feedback.Isolate Host: CRITICAL CONTAINMENT SUCCESS: SRV-BASTION-01 isolated via EDR. Because the attacker achieved Event 4624 (Logon Type 10) with elevated administrative privileges, host isolation severed their active interactive session and prevented lateral movement.
feedback.Block IP: PARTIAL SUCCESS: Blocked external IP 185.220.101.5 at the border. Note: Because an active session already succeeded (Event 4624), the attacker retained control unless host isolation or session termination occurred.
feedback.Escalate: ACCEPTABLE: Incident escalated to Tier 2 IR team. In a live breach with active privileged logon, immediate containment (Isolate Host) is best practice, but escalation prevented disaster.
feedback.Dismiss: CATASTROPHIC BREACH: Dismissed an active root/service account takeover! Adversary utilized SeBackupPrivilege to dump the Active Directory NTDS.dit database and pivot domain-wide.

educational_rationale.topic: Windows Security Auditing & Brute-Force / Credential Stuffing
educational_rationale.certification_relevance: Security+ SY0-701 (Section 2.4 Authentication & Authorization Attacks, Section 4.2 Incident Response Playbooks) & Network+ (Section 4.1 Remote Access Protocols - RDP Port 3389)
educational_rationale.deep_dive: Windows Event ID 4625 records failed logons. Note SubStatus 0xC000006A (bad password) and 0xC0000234 (account lockout). Logon Type 10 specifically indicates 'RemoteInteractive' (Terminal Services / RDP), while Logon Type 3 indicates network share/SMB. The critical turning point is Event ID 4624 (Logon Success) immediately following the failure burst, paired with Event ID 4672 (Special Privileges assigned, like SeBackupPrivilege). This signifies a confirmed breach requiring immediate containment.
